# `tdd stub <TEST-ID>`

Writes throwing stubs so `tdd red` is a real, non-weak Red. Stubs only fill in missing files/functions (real code is never touched). Arity comes from the call site and the return type from the compared literal (`== 3`, `, "s")`, `.is_err()`), falling back to `int`/`i64`/`any`; if the stub does not compile, write it by hand. An unknown REQ on the test is refused when specs exist.

New Java/PHP/C#/Julia stub files receive unique `CODE-…-STUB-…` annotations implementing the selected test's REQs **before Red**, so replacing a generated subject does not edit its test's oracle hash (#201). Keep or replace those annotations with the real CODE IDs. For handwritten production skeletons, add CODE/@implements before Red too: an unannotated dependency is protected support, not automatically production. Promotion after Red is refused with an ownership diagnostic; restore annotated failing code, record a fresh Red, then implement/Green. Never annotate genuine oracles as production to bypass the hash.

- **ts/js/py**: throwing stubs for the test's missing relative imports. JS/TS also reads multi-line and `import type`/inline `type` imports (types become `export type X = any`), `import * as ns` (`ns.fn(` → exported functions), static calls `Foo.create(` (→ `static create`), and names the test never calls (`CONFIG.max`, `initialState`) become a throwing `Proxy` value instead of a function. Bare package imports that resolve to a workspace package (package.json `name`/`main`/`exports`) or tsconfig path are stubbed in that entry file; unresolvable ones are listed under `! not stubbed:`. Methods are added to an **existing** class only when the receiver is provably that class (`new X().m(`, `v = new X(); v.m(`, a helper that returns only `new X(..)`, `X.m(`); otherwise nothing is added to real code.
- **JS/TS scope (#153)**: namespace members, methods and dynamic imports come only from the shared preamble and selected test, never sibling tests. `v = new Factory().create()` does not make `v` a Factory instance. Missing manifest-declared workspace entries (including conditional/subpath exports) are created at that entry path. In `assert.throws/rejects`, only the expected-error constructor argument implies Error inheritance; the subject under test remains an ordinary class.
- **Python**: skips stdlib and installed packages (including user-site/PYTHONPATH ones); names used in `pytest.raises`/`assertRaises`/`except` become `class X(Exception)`; a module that still holds only stubs gets newly imported names appended.
- **Python submodules (#158)**: `from pkg import api as local` creates `pkg/api.py` from calls to `local` in the selected test only, never sibling calls; the package initializer is left unchanged.
- **Go** (`go test` finds `undefined: X`): `NewX` constructors (`*X`), types, struct-literal fields, methods and fields (up to 4 probe passes); bare `New()` creates type `Pkg`; field access on a returned value creates `<Func>Result` structs. Constructors (`New`, `NewX`) return a zero value (`return &X{}[, nil]`) so only behaviour methods panic and the Red is not setup-origin. `Err*` sentinels become `var ErrX = errors.New("ErrX")` (also for an external `package x_test`, where the stub goes into the imported package and the in-package pass is skipped). The result is compile-checked with `go test -run ^$`; a failing check prints a warning instead of claiming success.
- **Go preservation (#161)**: external-package stubs always allocate a fresh noncolliding filename, preserving existing real and previously generated `_stub.go` files. Existing production `package` declarations determine the generated package name, not directory names or import aliases; compiler-qualified method types use that same package.
- **Rust** (`tests/*.rs` → `src/lib.rs`): free functions and, for capitalised imports, types (`enum` for `Name::Variant`, else a unit struct); `use crate::a::b::{…}` creates missing `src/a.rs`, `src/a/b.rs` and the `pub mod` lines; `use member_crate::a::X` goes into that workspace crate; `== Some(...)`/tuple literals give `Option<…>` returns. Struct fields are inferred only from struct literals; other field access needs a hand-written stub (the Red is rejected as a compile error until then). Red reasons show the panic message.
- **Java** (`Cls.method(` → `src/Cls.java` / `src/main/java`): `new X(a, b)` ctors (typed from literals) and `X.CONST` enums. Instance methods called on `new X(..)` objects (`a.balance()`) are stubbed too.
- **C/C++** (missing `#include "x.h"` → header-only stub; names from compiler diagnostics): headers go into `include/`/`src/` (never shadowing from `tests/`); unknown `foo_t` types get an opaque `typedef struct foo foo_t;`; typed pointer params come from declarations. Stubs are header-only, so drop the missing `.c`/`.cpp` from your build command.
- **C#** (#136, needs the `dotnet` SDK and a test csproj above the test file): `dotnet build` diagnostics are the source of truth — `CS0246`/`CS0103` (missing type), `CS0234` (missing namespace of a `using`), `CS0117`/`CS1061` (missing static/instance member), `CS0019` (operator). Only diagnostics inside the requested test (shared preamble + that test's lines) drive the stubs, in up to 8 build rounds. Types go into the referenced non-test project that matches the `using` namespace (else the only/best-named referenced project, else the test project with a `!` note), one `<Type>.cs` each, marked `// sdd-stub`: exception types (`: System.Exception`), enums (`X.Member`), records (`new X(a: 1)` named args), interfaces (`IFoo`), static classes (`X.Of(..)`) and classes (`new X(..)`, constructor takes `params dynamic[]` so setup never throws); members are `dynamic` (properties with `set` when assigned, `Async` methods return `Task<dynamic>`, factory names `Of/Create/From*/Parse/Zero/…` return their own type) and throw `NotImplementedException`. Real (unmarked) types are never edited: a missing member is reported as `! not stubbed`. The result is `compile-checked` only when the whole build passes. If only OTHER tests of the same project still fail to compile it says `NOT compile-checked` and names the first error (stub those tests next; one project = one compilation); if `dotnet build` cannot run (restore/network) nothing is claimed and nothing is generated. Build errors in referenced production projects (not the test) must be fixed by hand first.
- **PHP / Julia / R**: writes the file the test loads (`require_once`/`include`/`source`) with throwing functions (`LogicException` / `error()` / `stop()`) for unknown calls; PHP also generates classes from `Class::method(`/`new Class` and skips reserved words and `assert*` helpers.
- **JS/TS/Python classes** also get throwing methods for `new C().m(` / `v = C(); v.m(` calls; Java and Rust also get instance methods (Rust: `impl Type` with `new`-style constructors returning `Self`). PHP/C stubs skip classes, functions and types already declared in project files (and PHP built-ins); PHP exception classes extend `\Exception`. Go skips `any` receivers.
- **#107-#118 additions**: existing JS/TS modules get missing exports/consts/class methods appended (existing lines untouched); Python `from pkg import mod` creates `pkg/mod.py`; Go external `_test` packages are stubbed in the imported package dir; Rust stubs use `unimplemented!("T::m")`, `&mut self` and Result/Option returns; Java skips JDK classes, supports `250L`, Maven `gate --changed` uses `-am -amd`; C stubs `(void)` unused params; PHP `use Ns\Cls;` creates PSR-4 files (composer.json `autoload.psr-4`, else `src/`) and `--missing-module` accepts `Class "X" not found`.
- **#130/#131 (honest verdict, scoped, typed)**: stubs cover only the requested test (shared preamble + that test's body). The result line says `compile-checked` only when the compiler confirmed it (Rust: `cargo test --no-run`; C: `cc -fsyntax-only`); otherwise it says `compile NOT verified` (Java, PHP, Julia, ...) or prints the first compile error and `could not fully stub` — never "Red-safe". If `tdd red` still reports a load/compile error, finish the stub by hand (stub is not re-run in a loop). Languages without a generator (e.g. C#) print `nothing to stub`.
  - **Rust**: inline paths (`krate::geo::Point { x: 1 }`) create the module + a struct whose fields are typed from the literal values.
  - **Rust (#278/#280)**: `include!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), ..))` is a build.rs artifact (skipped for ownership; the oracle depends on `build.rs`). `assert!(f(..))` gives a `bool` return; items inside an existing inline `#[cfg(test)]` module are not treated as defined. Constructs the generator cannot produce (see #288 below) stay a `!` note on compile failure, naming what to write by hand.
  - **Rust (#288)**: return types are also inferred from `.len()`/`.is_empty()` (`Vec<i64>`), indexing (`f(..)["k"]` → `HashMap<String, V>`, `[0]` → `Vec<V>`), `>`/`<` comparisons, and `assert_eq!` against `Some(&x)`/`Some(..)`/`Ok(..)`/`Ok(())`/`Err(..)`/imported enum or struct values (`Option<&'static T>`, `Result<T, E>`). `impl Trait for X { type A = ..; const C: T = ..; fn m(..) }` in the test generates `pub trait Trait` with those associated types/consts/signatures (types the signatures name must resolve in the trait's module). Explicit generic args (`Log<A, 'a>`, `Log::<A>::new()`) generate `struct Log<T0, 'a>` (PhantomData) + `impl<..>`; a turbofish `f::<u8>(..)` generates `fn f<T>(_a0: impl Sized)`. A root-level imported macro (`use krate::m;`, `krate::m!`, `#[macro_use] extern crate`) gets `#[macro_export] macro_rules! m { ($($t:tt)*) => { unimplemented!("m!") } }` in that crate's `lib.rs`. Builder chains `Type::builder().a(1).b(2).build()` give every link but the last a by-value `self -> Self` method that throws. Still hand-written (the `!` note remains): macros imported from a nested module, enum generics, trait bounds/default methods, traits only called (not implemented) by the test, a macro whose result is used as a value, and call arities that differ between sites.
  - **Java**: `T v = X.m(..)` / `assertEquals(Enum.K, x.m())` give the return type; static factories (`of/create/from/zero/..`) return their own class; every call arity becomes an overload; `X.class`/`catch (X`/`assertThrows` exception classes extend `RuntimeException`; `a.f(..).g()` chains get an `<F>Result` class; classes imported from the project's own package are stubbed into that package; methods missing on an existing class are reported as `! not stubbed`, not silently ignored.
  - **C**: argument types come from casts, `&x`, arrays and declarations; `T *v` + `v->f` makes `T` a complete struct (`long f`); pointer results use the declared `T *` for `_t` opaque types.
  - **PHP**: `use PHPUnit\...`/vendor-autoloadable classes are never stubbed; classes used only in `catch`/`throw new` extend `\Exception`; instance methods called on `new C(..)` receivers (`$h->m()`) are stubbed.
  - **Julia**: `using .Mod` wraps the stub file in `module Mod` with `export`; `@test_throws X` creates `struct X <: Exception end`; test-local functions/destructured names and names defined by existing included files are not stubbed.
  - **Python**: for `eng, log = make()` only the tuple slot holding the class instance (`return Eng(..), log`) gets methods; new modules honor pytest `pythonpath` (`pytest.ini`/`pyproject.toml`/`setup.cfg`/`tox.ini`) even if that directory is new.
  - **#147 Python**: all names (classes, exceptions, constants, methods) come from the requested test's scope only (never other tests of the file); a variable rebound to another class (`s = Counter()` … `s = Sub()`) belongs to its latest class; a helper that returns an instance of class X gives methods only to X (other classes built inside the helper get none).
  - **#148 Go**: scoped to the requested test (compile errors for names it does not use are ignored); methods called through a field selector (`r.c.Add(2, 3)`) keep their arguments; bare `New()` returns the type the test names (`*pkg.Store` in a signature/helper parameter) instead of a package-derived one; external-package struct literals keep every field; a stub file holding only methods is reported, never "nothing to stub".
  - **#298 Rust**: a module that `include!`s a file or invokes macros only gets the items cargo reports missing (never a duplicate type); `T::default()` adds no `fn default` when `T` derives/implements `Default`; `Type::CONST`/`Type::f()` on an existing enum are added as `impl` items, not variants.
  - **#298/#304 Rust (r17a)**: nested struct literals give structs with typed fields (tuples, `Option`, `Vec`, arrays, suffixed numbers, nested structs); missing methods / associated fns on an **existing** (also generic) type are added to its impl from cargo's E0599 (an `impl<..> T<..>` is created when the type has none); UFCS calls (`<T as Tr>::f(..)`, `Tr::f(&x)` with `x` visibly another type) make `Tr` a trait plus `impl Tr for T`; empty-collection / `None` arguments (`checksum(&[])`) take a concrete type (`&[u8]`, or the element type of another call) instead of an uninferable `A0`; consts/tables compared (`assert_eq!(T[0], (1, 2))`) or iterated (`for (a, b) in T`) get tuple/`Option`/`&[..]` types; `tdd stub A B ...` / `tdd stub A --all` stub several tests of one file in one run (a single ID still stubs only its own test). Names the file imports with a root-level `use` for other tests are stubbed too so the file compiles (module-path imports of other tests are still left alone); enum variants take typed fields (nested literals, tuples, `Option`, `Vec`); a trait used through `&dyn T` / `S: T` / `impl T` gets the methods the test calls on it; a value returned by an associated fn that the test compares with a literal is not the type itself, so its methods (`contains`, `matches`, ..) are not added to the type. Not changed: constructors (`new`, `default`, ..) keep their non-throwing body by design (#103/#288), so a setup call never makes the Red weak.
  - **#149 Rust/Java/C++**: Rust `Type::new(..).unwrap()` returns `Result<Self, String>`, calls compared with `None`/`Some(x)` return `Option<_>`. Java: commas inside string/char literals are not argument separators; `assertEquals("lit", C.m(..))` returns `String`; chained static factories (`A.standard().analyze(..)`) get a `<F>Result` class (a list when `.get/.stream/.size` is chained); generic element types (`List<Token>`) are stubbed; generated stubs start with `// sdd-stub:` and later `tdd stub` runs extend them. C++: `ns::Cls v(..); v.m(..)` yields `namespace ns { class Cls {..}; }` with variadic throwing methods (variables are never functions); a C/C++ stub that still does not compile exits 1.
  - **#150 PHP / C#**: PHP project-class detection is namespace-aware (`use App\Query\Parser;` is stubbed at `src/Query/Parser.php` even if `App\Sdl\Parser` exists; `tdd red --missing-module` compares the FQCN); `Cls::CONST` creates a class with `public const`, `Enum::CASE->value` a string-backed `enum` with those cases (plus static methods called on it). C# stubs go into the namespace of the project the test `using`s / is named after (the test's own `.Tests` namespace is stripped), never the test namespace; a type seen as a helper return/parameter/`is X`/`typeof(X)` is a `class`, not a `static class`; `CS1501` (LINQ-name collisions such as `Append`/`Count` on an `IEnumerable` stub) adds the member; our own exception stubs accept members (`ex.Line`); "not stubbed" notes are de-duplicated. **C# limits**: generic types/methods (`Parser<T>`) are not stubbed (one such field in a shared preamble blocks every test of the class — hand-write the skeleton); members are `dynamic`, so lambdas on a stubbed result (`.Select(x => ..)`, CS1977) and `with` expressions (CS8858) do not compile — hand-write typed stubs there.
  - **#151 Julia / TS / JS**: Julia names ending in `!` are stubbed; a missing function of an already-existing *stub-only* included file is appended inside its `module` (and `export`ed) — real code is never edited and is reported instead; the `module` name follows the `using .X` named like the missing include (not the first `using`). TS/JS: names already reachable through a barrel's `export * from` / `export { x } from` are not stubbed over; `new C<T>(..)` counts like `new C(..)`; methods are only stubbed for receivers that really hold the class (`const { b, out } = mk()` with `return { b: new Box(), out }` stubs `b` only, not `out.push`); names ending in `Error`/`Exception` (or used in `toThrow(X)`) become `class X extends Error`; `import * as ns from '../src/ns.js'` no longer invents an `export const js`.
- **#288 Python**: a name imported but used only as an annotation (`r: Rng`, `-> Rng`) is stubbed as `class X(Protocol)`; `from` imports inside `conftest.py` fixtures the test can use are stubbed too; a test that runs a subprocess (`subprocess.run(["node", "cli.ts"])`) gets a note (the external program is not generated; `tdd red` accepts its genuine non-zero exit/assertion failure without `--weak`); "nothing to stub" reports how many relative/absolute/conftest `from` imports were checked (plain `import x` is not checked).
- **Known limits**: C `enum`/full `typedef`s are not stubbed (only opaque/field-accessed `_t` structs); Go `[]byte(x)` params stay `any`; Rust enum payload variants are stubbed as unit; Python attributes on helper-built objects are not stubbed.
- **#163/#168 PHP / C#**: C# csproj ownership and ProjectReference discovery work without Git. PHP reads the installed Composer ClassLoader PSR-4 mappings, including local path packages; before installation, declared local path repositories (including wildcard URLs) supply mappings from their package manifests. Symlinked vendor paths resolve to their project source. External/vendor-only destinations are explicitly declined. A throwing PHPUnit subject reached before the assertion counter increments is executed Red, not a skipped test; mixed passing/skipped provider rows are accepted.
- **#169 Julia**: comma-separated relative imports (`using .Existing, .Fresh`) select/wrap the matching included module. The binding probe loads non-relative imports in the project environment, so imported stdlib functions such as `LinearAlgebra.dot` and `issymmetric` are not shadowed with throwing stubs.
- **#176 ownership**: Java explicit imports distinguish fully qualified classes even when another project package declares the same basename. PHP aliases generate the imported class's actual name at its PSR-4 destination; relative and absolute local Composer path repositories resolve to the same package. Julia follows literal transitive includes (cycle-safe, within the project), preserving existing definitions instead of shadowing them in a new stub module.
- **#192 binding ownership**: Java project wildcard imports resolve existing classes before generation; ambiguous wildcard bindings are diagnosed and never shadowed. PHP grouped/aliased imports use the same PSR-4 resolver as ordinary imports. C# existing-type lookup is restricted to visible namespaces and the test project's transitive ProjectReferences; an unrelated same-named type cannot suppress a missing stub.
- **#194 C/C++ probes**: use the matching `compile_commands.json` entry (test directory, project root or `build/`) when available, preserving compiler, working directory, include/define/language flags and removing compile/output/dependency-file arguments. Otherwise use the nearest declared CMake language standard (`CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD`/`CMAKE_C_STANDARD` or `cxx_std_*`/`c_std_*`) plus generic include paths. Complex generator expressions/toolchain flags still require a compilation database or hand-written code checked by the owning build. A successful no-op probe says `nothing to stub ... (compile-checked)`, not that valid C++20 source is broken.
- **#202 Rust workspace discovery**: imported member crates are discovered from local Cargo manifests even without Git; missing modules/functions are generated in the owning member while existing libraries are preserved.
- **#222 PHP functions/enums**: `use function Ns\f` / `use const Ns\C` create throwing functions and placeholder consts in `<PSR-4 root>/functions.php` (namespace-correct; appended to an existing stub-only file) and register it under `composer.json` `autoload.files` (run `composer dump-autoload` if `vendor/` exists). A CamelCase `Cls::Case`, or any `Cls::CASE->member`, makes `Cls` a string-backed `enum` with that `case`; `Cls::Case->m()` adds a throwing instance method.
- **#224 R**: names defined in the test directory's `helper*.R` / `setup*.R` (autoloaded by testthat) are never stubbed; when every `source()`d file exists, missing functions are appended to a stub-only one (real code is reported as `! not stubbed`).
- **#221 C++**: `using ns::sub::Type;` places an unqualified `Type` (constructed or called as `Type::f(`) in `namespace ns::sub`.
- **#214/#215/#218/#219**: Python: a namespace dir (no `__init__.py`) satisfies only submodules it holds (other names get an `__init__.py`), `__init__` re-exports count as defined, and `pkg.sql` + `pkg.sql.ast` imports create `pkg/sql/__init__.py` (never `sql.py` beside `sql/`); Go: a member called as a method anywhere in the test file is never also a struct field; C#: `global using` in other test-project files drives namespace stubs; JS: `require()` stubs get `module.exports` (relative or workspace package) and `await import()` of workspace packages stubs the members used on the namespace.
- **Elixir / ExUnit**: `tdd stub` writes `lib/<snake_case path>.ex` with `defmodule M do` and throwing `def f(_a1, ..), do: raise("not implemented: f")` for modules the test `alias`/`import`/`use`/`require`s or calls as `Mod.fun(..)` (arity from the call; `import Mod` also stubs bare calls). Stdlib/ExUnit/known library modules and modules already defined in `lib/` or `test/support/` are skipped; missing defs are appended to an existing stub-only module, real code is only reported. Stub files get a `# @id CODE-…-STUB-…` annotation like Java/PHP/C#/Julia.
- **#240 Julia**: `tdd stub` resolves `include(joinpath(@__DIR__, "..", "src", "X.jl"))` like the literal relative include.
- **#281/#282**: a newly created JS/TS stub carries `@id CODE-…-STUB-NNN @implements REQ-…` (swapping in the real implementation is not an ownership change); `tdd red` classifies by exception type — an AssertionError (even embedding subprocess stderr such as "Cannot find module") is an assertion, and ENOENT/FileNotFoundError on a `deliverables` path that does not exist yet is a valid Red.
  - **#290 Rust**: a variant the test uses that an existing enum lacks is added to it; an inline `#[cfg(test)]` test gets an explanatory `!` note; new Rust stub files carry `// @id CODE-…-STUB-NNN @implements REQ-…`; an unchanged `lib.rs` is never reported as stubbed. Still by hand: call-only traits, generic enums, arity differing across call sites, `entry!`-style macros, tuple structs, `&mut self` inference, consts, closure-param arity, test-local trait imports.
- **#291** Python: new stub files carry `# @id CODE-…-STUB-NNN @implements REQ-…`; `from pkg import mod` used as `mod.f()` stubs `pkg/mod.py` (not `def mod`); a helper module next to the test file is never duplicated under `src/`; a stub that throws at pytest collection (e.g. in `parametrize` args) gets a hint to build those values inside the test.
- **#309 (r21c)** design decisions:
  - **Throwing constructors are opt-in**: `.sdd/config.json` `"stubThrowingConstructors": true` makes JS/TS (non-Error) and Java class constructors throw `not implemented: X`; the default stays non-throwing (tests #103/#288 rely on construction succeeding). Python/Rust/C# are unchanged.
  - **TS error hierarchy**: when the test asserts the same subject `instanceof` two error classes from the same import (`toBeInstanceOf(NotFoundError)` and `toBeInstanceOf(AppError)`), the one with a generic stem (`App`/`Base`/`Domain`/`Api`/`Http`/…) or a name that is a suffix of the other becomes the parent and is declared first. Anything else stays flat `extends Error`.
  - **Java**: same-arity calls with different declared result types (`int a = c.f(1); String b = c.f("x")`) get typed overloads (literal param types) instead of one `Object` signature; `Outer.Inner` becomes a nested `static class`, or an `enum` when `Outer.Inner.K` is used.
  - **ExUnit DSL macros**: after `use Mod` (Mod undefined), paren-less calls like `rule :a do .. end` / `check_ok 1, 2` become throwing `defmacro`s of Mod (arity = args + do-block) and `__using__` does `import Mod`; the macro expands to `raise "not implemented: f"`, so the test is a real Red, not a compile error.
  - Not reproduced / skipped: crash-class Red for Rust stubs (no minimal repro; #217 already rejects signal/exit crashes), remaining F7/F9 items (the report is not available).
  - **Rust stub (#310)**: consts beside a float literal (`EPSILON / 2.0`, `assert_eq!(X, 1e-5)`) are `f64`; `Name::new(&v, ..)` is a constructor, not a UFCS trait call; `<T as Trait>::Assoc` makes `Trait` a trait with `type Assoc` (impl'd for `T` as `i64`); `&mut self` is also inferred when the call sits in `assert*!(s.m(..))` on a `let mut` receiver; enums get an inherent `impl` for methods called on `let x = Enum::Variant(..)` values. Skipped as risky/ambiguous (finish by hand): `macro_rules!` typed returns (`!`-typed `unimplemented!` macros), trait-import stubbing from method calls, lifetimes, `Box<dyn T>`-only traits, `Default` derive over non-Default fields, Option-vs-Result inference from `.is_none()`, async/`impl Future` signatures, attribute calls (Python `call`/`returncode`).
  - **CLI (#313)**: `tdd stub --all <ID>` now takes the ID (flag order no longer matters); usage lists the multi-ID/`--all` form; IDs from another test file are reported as "is in <file>, not <file>"; stubbing an unapproved T2/T3 feature is still allowed but prints a `!` warning that `tdd red` will refuse until approved. Skipped: workspace member without `src/lib.rs` (already covered by #304, no repro) and Python missing-name messages (report unavailable; ambiguous).

## Stub confidence (r24b, design §3.2)

- Every inferred Rust stub element has a confidence: `shown` (type literally in the test/source), `inferred` (from a call shape or comparison), `guessed` (no evidence).
- `tdd stub <ID> --report` prints `element | confidence | evidence` (evidence = first test line using the element). Guessed elements are also flagged with a `!` line even without `--report`.
- A `guessed` element is not emitted as a wrong concrete type. Rust consts with no evidence get `pub const X: () = (); // SDD-TODO(stub): type unknown` (instead of `i64 = 0`).
- Python and TS/JS: a const with no evidence gets a marker comment on its line (`X = None  # SDD-TODO(stub): ...`, `export const X: any = undefined; // SDD-TODO(stub): ...`) and is reported `guessed`; an evidenced one (Python `[]` const) is `inferred` and unmarked. Other output is byte-identical. TS class/function/Proxy value stubs are not marked: they are shape-only and throw by design.
- Rust `shown`: a const typed in the test (`let x: f64 = LIMIT;`, `LIMIT as f64`) and a fn whose return is annotated (`let n: usize = size(2);`). A free fn whose return type defaults to `i64` with no evidence is reported `guessed` (`! f: return type defaulted to i64 ...`) but the code is NOT changed and NOT marked. Methods are not reported (their types come from many shapes; not safe to classify).
- `tdd red` REJECTS a compile-class failure located in an `SDD-TODO(stub)` element (the error names it, or points at its file:line), saying to fill the type by hand; it is never accepted as a Red (also with `--weak`).
- Not done yet: free/instance fn return types still default to `i64` when nothing is known (changing that would alter existing supported output); Python/TS stubs carry no confidence markers.
